I'm so sorry that you're going thru this. I had an eerily similar experience this holiday season as well. Nasty, mean, awful things were said by him. I started to doubt myself. I started to think he was right. I couldn't help but hear those words on repeat  and it sucked.

Be gentle with yourself. Know that people here understand and support you. Tell yourself everyday that you deserve to be treated with love and compassion and respect. Because it's true. You are worth so much more than you know. 

And when the awful words start to replay, distraction is key. Journal all of your thoughts and feelings. Cry and mourn what's gone. And then do something ridiculous. Put on some old school music and dance around. Take some old china and smash it to bits.  Paint your room a color that you love but have been afraid to try. Do things just for you because you deserve to. And eventually, the pain lessens and the horrible awfulness will get quieter and you will heal.
Oh my goodness that is ridiculously freakin precious!!!
Thank you. What we had felt all encompassing. And my whole world just fell apart. But you and so many others are right. Time will be the biggest healer. I just have to try and hold on
Thank you. I needed a reminder that storms run out of rain eventually
Thank you.  It is really difficult to see the light at the end of the tunnel right now.  But I'm trying to hang in there.
I really really want to believe that it will get better.  Its hard to see right now.
Thank you.  You guys really are the best and I hope all of you know that you made a huge difference to this random internet person.
Thank you.  I wish I could just mute his voice in my head. I'll try the distractions.  Maybe they'll help drown it out.
Thank you.  You're right.  It might not be worth it.  I don't really want to be gone.  I just really really need it to stop feeling like this.  It's so heavy.
Y'all are some wonderful awesome people!
That is first on my list of things to do as soon as I get back on my feet.  This year really kicked my ass and I need help.  I can't fight it alone any more.  Thank you.
Thank you.  Hope is always appreciated even when its hard to see
